messages:

Subject: Post-call: NexaHealth integration & model-routing + policy config

Thanks for a productive call today — quick recap and next steps from our side.

Key takeaways:
- Primary use case: clinical triage assistant in the patient intake flow (low-latency responses required for UI flow).
- Expected QPS: ~60 sustained, spikes to 200 during morning rush.
- Data sensitivity: PHI scope limited to hashed patient identifiers; Nexa requires VPC/private deployment for production.
- Success metrics: 95th pct latency < 350ms for short prompts, cost target < $0.004/token equivalent.

Bundled asks we agreed on:
1) SDK/Auth: Nexa devs will evaluate SDK quickstart and want a service-account pattern for server-side calls (token rotation + KMS).
2) Integration: embed/reranker pipeline for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) — embeddings for candidate retrieval, then reranker for top-k scoring before generating structured tool-calls.
3) Model routing & policy config: need recommended policy for balancing latency vs cost (hot path -> low-latency variants in us-east, fallback chain to cheaper quantized variants; region routing for EU users later).
4) Eval plan: we’ll provide a small eval set (50 prompts) to validate reranker + structured output quality.

Attachments: I attached a draft model-routing policy and a short SDK setup guide for your engineers (see attachments).

Next steps (action owners):
- Nexa: share PII/PHI scoping confirmation and internal security contact (Sarah).
- Redwood (Dev): produce a sample SDK token exchange snippet + service account pattern by Mon 12/7.
- Redwood (Marcus): propose initial model routing policy that meets the latency/cost targets and a fallback chain for service continuity by Tue 12/8.
- Mutual: schedule a 60-min integration working session the week of 12/14 (invite to follow).

If that aligns, I’ll circulate the draft policy and a short integration checklist.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole

Hi Sarah / James — following up with concrete integration guidance and a proposed model-routing policy. See summary + code snippets below; full docs attached.

1) SDK & Auth (quickstart)\- Install: npm install @redwood-inference/sdk\- Env: export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<service-account-token>"\- Service account pattern: create a server-side service account, exchange long-lived key for short-lived tokens via our token-exchange endpoint. Example curl:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/token-exchange \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <LONG_LIVED_KEY>' \n  -d '{"scope": "inference:server", "ttl_seconds": 3600}'

(We’ll provide a small utility to call KMS and rotate keys; see attachment redwood_sdk_setup.md)

2) Embeddings / Reranker pattern\- Pipeline: user query -> retrieve candidates (your Pinecone) -> call Redwood reranker endpoint with candidates metadata and model selection -> top-k returned to generator for structured tool calling.

Reranker call example (pseudocode):
- endpoint: POST /v1/rerank\- body: {query: "...", candidates: [{id:.., text:..}, ...]}

Redwood reranker runs server-side (recommended) to avoid leaking candidate content to clients, and returns scores + normalized reasons. We can also provide a client-side scoring shim if you prefer.

3) Model routing & policy (proposal)
- Hot path: us-east-1 region -> low-latency model variant (gptx-lite-16b-llm) with GPU optimized exec; target 95th < 350ms for prompts < 512 tokens.
- Warm path: if cost optimization desired for non-interactive flows, route to quantized variants (gptx-q8-16b) with batching (2–4s latency).
- Fallback chain: primary (gptx-lite-16b in us-east) -> fallback to quantized variant in same region -> cross-region fallback to cheaper variant in us-west (if capacity constrained) -> predefined rate-limited throttle with a graceful degrade response and a link to cached answer if available.
- Policy controls: per-route latency_slo_ms, max_batch_size, fallback_order, cost_priority (low|balanced|low_cost). We’ll share a wire-format YAML for your infra team.

4) Structured output & tool calling\- Use schema-enforced structured responses for downstream systems (JSON schema validation). We recommend the tool-calling pattern for any actions (DB writes, EHR updates) where Redwood returns a validated tool invocation object rather than free-form text.

5) Next steps / asks\- Nexa to provide the redacted prompt set + security contact (EOD Mon 12/7).\- Nexa infra to confirm Pinecone namespace and whether we can access a staging vector project.\- Redwood to provide: (a) sample YAML policy + routing table (Marcus), (b) SDK token-exchange utility (Dev), (c) sample reranker integration snippet (attachment).

I’ve attached the draft routing policy and the SDK quickstart. Happy to hop on a call Wed/Thu to walk through the YAML and the reranker contract.

--
